title: Bug: `test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` doesn't teardown iptables to original state
author: Javier-Tan
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

When `kubesonic/test_k8s_join_disjoin.py` is run, there are some leftover config in `iptables` and `ip6tables`.

This could cause errors in `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` as it checks `iptables -S` and `ip6tables -S` for expected results (or similar tests that may use `iptables`/`ip6tables`).

Good to note `config reload` does reset the iptables, but is not guaranteed to run (and shouldn't be run just to teardown)

### Steps to Reproduce

On a clean DUT (config reloaded) run `iptables -S; ip6tables -S` OR `iptables-save; ip6tables-save`
Run `kubesonic/test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` test
run `iptables -S; ip6tables -S` OR `iptables-save; ip6tables-save` again
See difference

To see it causing test failures, run `kubesonic/test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` and `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` consecutively

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

`kubesonic/test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` should teardown to leave iptables as it was originally

### Relevant log output

```shell
`cacl/test_cacl_application.py` failure when running it after kubesonic test:

E       Failed: Unexpected iptables rules: {'-A KUBE-FIREWALL -m comment --comment "kubernetes firewall for dropping marked packets" -m mark --mark 0x8000/0x8000 -j DROP', '-A INPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL', '-N KUBE-FIREWALL', '-N KUBE-KUBELET-CANARY', '-A KUBE-FIREWALL ! -s 127.0.0.0/8 -d 127.0.0.0/8 -m comment --comment "block incoming localnet connections" -m conntrack ! --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED,DNAT -j DROP', '-A OUTPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL'}
```


comments.author: lixiaoyuner
comments.body: @Javier-Tan, wondering what's the conflict here, how this kubesonic test iptables rule affects the cacl/test_cacl_application.py, just want to know that is it possible to cause any issue in production when these two features are both enabled.

comments.author: Javier-Tan
comments.body:
@lixiaoyuner the leftover iptables from kubernetes test are unexpected in cacl test:

The Kubernetes iptable generated rules are generated during this command https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/bacd336b1b7a4d39217ddba9bf3cde96ac4716ee/tests/kubesonic/test_k8s_join_disjoin.py#L353 which has a proper teardown, but it doesn't get rid of the iptable rules

cacl test checks against a set of expected iptable rules https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/bacd336b1b7a4d39217ddba9bf3cde96ac4716ee/tests/cacl/test_cacl_application.py#L1081 

Which are generated by https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/bacd336b1b7a4d39217ddba9bf3cde96ac4716ee/tests/cacl/test_cacl_application.py#L497

I've had a search about removing the kubernetes generated iptable rules but it seems there is no straightforward way of doing it.
